content: Odevixibat is indicated for the treatment of pruritus associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) at a dose of 40 mcg/kg taken orally once daily in the morning. It is also indicated for pruritus associated with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) at a dose of 120 mcg/kg taken orally once daily in the morning. For patients aged 3 months or older with PFIC, the medication is approved; however, its safety and efficacy have not been established for patients under 3 months of age. Similarly, for ALGS, it is approved for patients aged 1 year or older, but its safety and efficacy have not been established for those under 1 year of age. When co-administered with bile acid sequestrants such as cholestyramine, colesevelam, or colestipol, the levels or effects of odevixibat may be reduced due to drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. To mitigate this interaction, it is recommended to administer bile acid sequestrants at least 4 hours before or after taking odevixibat. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. There is a pregnancy safety study in place to monitor outcomes in women exposed to odevixibat during pregnancy. Currently, there are no human data available to determine the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse developmental outcomes associated with the drug. However, no data are available on its presence in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. During lactation, odevixibat may reduce the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (FSVs). Therefore, FSV levels should be monitored, and intake should be increased if a deficiency occurs. The medication should be administered in the morning with a meal. For patients taking bile acid-binding resins, odevixibat should be taken at least 4 hours before or after the resin. Capsules should be swallowed whole with a glass of water and should not be crushed or chewed. For oral pellets, the contents of the shell should be mixed into soft food or liquid, and children should not swallow unopened shells containing the pellets. The medication should be stored at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted between 15–30°C (59–86°F). The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
